crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Invoice Capture and Coding
children.blurb: Invoice capture and coding covers the intake of supplier invoices and the assignment of general ledger codes, cost centres and tax treatments before payment runs.

children.name: Customer Credit Risk
children.blurb: Customer credit risk is the chance that a buyer will not pay what they owe on the terms agreed, and it sits at the centre of receivables work.

children.name: Programmable Settlement and Escrow
children.blurb: Programmable settlement and escrow covers the use of software rules and smart contracts to hold funds and release them automatically when agreed conditions are met.

children.name: Collections and Payment Plans
children.blurb: Collections and payment plans cover the work of recovering money owed on overdue invoices and arranging structured schedules for customers who cannot pay in full on time.

children.name: Working Capital Timing
children.blurb: Working capital timing is the practice of managing when cash leaves and enters a business, chiefly through the gap between paying suppliers and collecting from customers.

sections.body: Payables and receivables is the money in and money out side of a business, the invoices a company owes and the invoices it is owed. Artificial intelligence is now doing the reading work that used to consume accounts payable teams, pulling line items, tax amounts and purchase order numbers out of scanned invoices and matching them to the right ledger codes. On the receivables side it scores customers by payment behaviour and outside signals to flag who is likely to pay late or not at all. It also sits inside settlement and collections workflows, deciding when to release funds, when to send a reminder and what payment plan a struggling customer can realistically carry. The work is unglamorous and mostly invisible, which is exactly where it tends to stick.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Invoice capture is the most mature part of this field. Modern systems handle clean digital invoices well and cope with moderate variation in layout, but messy scans, unusual formats and ambiguous line items still need a human. Credit risk models are useful as a second opinion rather than a verdict, and they inherit whatever bias sits in the historical payment data they learn from. Programmable settlement is technically workable but legally and operationally uneven, because money movement touches banking rules, escrow law and counterparty trust that no model can settle on its own. Collections is the hardest area, since a model can rank who to call but cannot make a customer pay, and aggressive automation can damage a relationship that a human conversation would have saved. Working capital timing is where the numbers get genuinely hard, because the benefit depends on forecasts of when money actually arrives, not when it is due.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages run roughly in the order money moves through a company. Invoice Capture and Coding is the entry point, covering how documents become structured data and how coding decisions get made or corrected. Customer Credit Risk follows, dealing with who is on the other side of the invoice and how their likelihood of paying gets estimated. Programmable Settlement and Escrow sits in the middle, covering the mechanics and the constraints of moving money automatically once terms are met. Collections and Payment Plans handles what happens when payment does not arrive on time, including how outreach and repayment schedules get prioritised. Working Capital Timing closes the loop, tying the whole cycle to the cash position of the business. A reader new to the area should start with invoice capture, while anyone already handling receivables will get more from the credit risk and collections pages.
